## Episode Thesis

Folksam chief economist Marcus Svedberg criticises the Swedish election campaign for economic populism. In his view the parties are competing on household-budget handouts such as the food VAT cut, even though the Swedish economy is doing well and does not need stimulus. He argues the debate should cover structural issues instead: a broad energy agreement covering nuclear and wind, AI regulation and its effect on the labour market, and a long-term tax reform. No listed equities are discussed in investment terms; the only company names are the guest's employer, the host's media outlet and advertisers.
